introduction: At this level, we will understand the two most fundamental metrics of national income: GDP and GNP. The primary difference between them lies entirely in two words: 'Boundary' and 'Citizenship'.

core_concepts.title: GDP (Gross Domestic Product)
core_concepts.description: GDP is the total monetary value of all 'final goods and services' produced within the 'domestic territory' of a country in a given financial year. It does not matter WHO produces it (an Indian citizen or a foreign company); as long as it is produced within India's geographical boundaries, it is counted in India's GDP.

core_concepts.title: GNP (Gross National Product)
core_concepts.description: GNP is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced by the 'citizens' (nationals) of a country in a given financial year, regardless of where they are in the world. (Formula: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad).

core_concepts.title: NFIA (Net Factor Income from Abroad)
core_concepts.description: NFIA is the difference between the money earned by Indians working abroad and the money earned by foreigners working in India. If Indians bring in more money than foreigners take out, NFIA is positive, and GNP > GDP. (For India, historically, NFIA is usually negative because outgoing foreign profits exceed incoming remittances).

core_concepts.title: Final Goods vs. Intermediate Goods
core_concepts.description: When calculating GDP/GNP, only 'Final Goods' (ready for consumption) are counted. 'Intermediate goods' (raw materials like steel bought to make a car, or flour bought by a baker) are strictly excluded to avoid the massive error of 'Double Counting'.

important_entities.name: Domestic Territory
important_entities.significance: In economics, the 'Domestic Territory' is not just the landmass. Indian embassies located in foreign countries, Indian naval ships, and Air India flights operating in international airspace are legally considered part of India's 'Domestic Territory' for GDP calculation.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic exam question: 'If an American company (like Apple) manufactures iPhones in India, where is its income added?' Answer: Because the production happened inside India's borders, it is added to India's 'GDP'. However, because the company is foreign, that profit is subtracted out and will NOT be included in India's 'GNP'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: When you see 'D' (Domestic), only look at the geographical land. When you see 'N' (National), only look at the citizenship/passport of the producer.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the core formula: GNP = GDP + NFIA. If a country is a closed economy (no imports/exports), then GDP = GNP.
